data.body:
# PR #120 / #121 evaluation -> two design epics (provider seam + Jira Data Center)

## What was asked
Evaluate GitHub PRs #120 (Jira Data Center reconciler adapter) and #121 (OpenAI-compatible LLM
endpoint for Bedrock) against rebar's design/ADRs/docs, choosing per PR between accept-as-is,
modify, counter-epic, or reject-with-rationale. Then run /rebar-brainstorm per feature and record
an epic for each. PR code reuse was explicitly optional/low-priority.

## PR verdicts delivered
- **#121 (LLM)**: modify before acceptance + a small follow-up. It closes a gap rebar deliberately
  parked (commit 75e598a41 added the base_url/api_key refusal as "a capability gap ... surfaced not
  hidden"), and docs/llm-framework.md:126-133,226 already documented the capability as working while
  runner.py:653 refused it. But it branched on cfg.base_url BEFORE provider inference (a fourth
  implicit provider selector that overrides REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER), silently disabled prompt
  caching / transport retry / read timeout, and left signed-verdict provenance falsifiable.
- **#120 (Jira DC)**: counter-epic, not review rounds. It rides ADR 0035's Backend port correctly but
  imports adapters/jira privates cross-package, forks map_fields_to_remote from
  adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72 with one line changed, never adds itself to the backend contract
  suite (fixture params are ["fake","jira"]), inherits creation_channel="jira" silently
  (apply_inbound_records.py:163; CREATION_CHANNELS is a closed frozenset at reducer/_version.py:160),
  and its resolve_assignee consults a `_assignee_resolver` attribute nothing ever sets -> the
  authoritative branch is unreachable, guaranteeing assignee-diff churn.

## Research that changed the design (both epics)
- pydantic-ai already ships the seam: `infer_model(provider_factory=...)` (upstream directs
  user-configurable-provider apps there, issue #1343) and `ModelProfile` for per-vendor capabilities.
  So rebar should adopt upstream contracts rather than invent `ModelCapabilities`/`force_prompted`.
- pydantic-ai has a NATIVE BedrockConverseModel with BedrockModelSettings prompt caching -> no
  gateway needed; PR #121's gateway approach gives up caching. Caveat: pydantic-ai#4381 reports
  caching silently failing with inference-profile ARNs, which is also AWS's throttling mitigation.
- aider/OpenHands delegate breadth to LiteLLM-as-SDK but still keep per-provider capability layers
  (OpenHands model_features.py). Rejected in-process LiteLLM: its normalization drifts on exactly
  what rebar depends on (cache semantics, tool-call shapes, cost accounting).
- **Jira DC is EOL**: no new purchases since 2026-03-30, no new features, read-only 2029-03-28, and
  **no DC trial licenses issuable since 2026-03-30**. No official DC OpenAPI spec exists (WADL only;
  JRASERVER-65954/68539 open) -> spec-driven contract testing unavailable.
- Verification oracle: pycontribs/jira publishes `pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` (port 2990,
  documented creds). 8.17.1 >= 8.14 so PAT bearer auth is genuinely exercised.

## Decisions taken by the operator during brainstorm
1. Provider support: two first-class (Anthropic, Bedrock) + best-effort rest; dogfood Bedrock on the
   AWS-hosted review bot, still Claude models, routed via Bedrock.
2. Bot Bedrock auth: raise IMDS hop limit to 2 on the existing instance role (no new secret).
3. Availability: Bedrock-only, NO cross-provider fallback (a fallback would mask the failures the
   dogfooding exists to surface); mitigate inside Bedrock + alarm on VOTER_ERROR.
4. Verdict provenance: still sign on every tier, but stamp provider/endpoint/tier/capabilities.
5. Jira DC is a real CMS need; build it behind a parameterized Jira-family seam.
6. Jira family shares ONE `jira` provenance identity; disambiguate via RemoteRef.instance.
7. DC transport depends on pycontribs/jira, ONLY under a jira-datacenter extra, and must not alter
   or replace the live-validated Cloud/ACLI path.
8. Extraction is allowed but Cloud must be frozen with characterization tests FIRST.

## Tickets created
- Epic **061c-ecd1-8967-4a76** (disparaged-gratuitous-rooster) — LLM provider seam. Children:
  7468 (S1 provider factory), f184 (S2 ModelProfile capabilities), 2932 (S3 native Bedrock),
  dc0d (S4 OpenAI-compatible), 343b (S5 tiered provenance), 0d76 (S6 Bedrock parity run),
  9249 (S7 Bedrock IAM/credentials), eb6e (S8 bot cutover), 8625 (S9 ADR+docs).
- Epic **e369-a449-4773-48fb** (adroit-deductible-kakapo) — Jira DC via a Jira-family seam. Children:
  acb2 (J1 characterization freeze), 62d9 (J2 extract jira_family), aac8 (J3 RichTextCodec),
  0a94 (J4 UserIdentityModel), c97f (J5 Docker harness), 9fd4 (J6 pycontribs transport),
  b4e3 (J7 assemble + contract suite), 8c35 (J8 ADR amending 0035).
- **9895-ac7d-4276-4f08** — idea, linked relates_to e369: live-validate DC against the real client
  instance when sandbox access exists (kept out of the epic because its precondition is access we
  don't control, which would fail the measurability criterion).
All children linked with blocks edges; file_impact recorded on every ticket.

## Plan-review state at stop
- 7468 (S1): **certified**.
- acb2 (J1): **certified**.
- 9249 (S7): PASSED on substance, then my own post-PASS edits (title alignment + operator-attested
  sweep) made it **stale-material**; the re-run returned INDETERMINATE.
- c97f (J5): **unsigned** — last completed review was a BLOCK whose 5 findings are all now fixed in
  the description; subsequent re-runs produced empty output.
- Cause of the failures: `rebar.llm.anthropic_model: llm transport retry` warnings in stderr — the
  Anthropic API was erroring/rate-limiting. Environmental, NOT a plan defect. Running several
  reviews concurrently made it worse, and a concurrent `review-plan --status` call blocked ~10min on
  a lock.

## Gate findings that changed the plans (the gate earned its keep)
1. S1: pydantic-ai's provider_factory returns only a Provider — no channel for the retrying
   httpx.AsyncClient to reach teardown at runner.py:446-452. Fixed with a per-run ProviderSession
   owning closeable lifetime.
2. S1: tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:33 and test_transport_retry.py:28 import
   _build_retrying_anthropic_model from rebar.llm.runner — an unenumerated migration surface.
3. S7: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml has NO networks: section (gerrit/review-bot/opcert share one
   bridge), so the proposed iptables IMDS containment was unimplementable.
4. S7: the opcert container legitimately uses IMDS (docker-compose.yml:157-158) — the containment
   would have broken it, AND it contradicts the premise that hop limit must be raised. S7 now
   measures first with a pre-decided contingency.
5. S7: infra/terraform/iam.tf:4-9 declares a SINGLE-OWNER CONTRACT — downstream stories add
   iam_s<N>.tf, never edit iam.tf. Retargeted to iam_s7.tf.
6. J5: challenged whether a licensed Jira image still exists post-Server-EOL — research produced the
   pinned pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 answer.
7. J5: the teardown oracle violated ADR 0037 §3 (no post-deletion search-index assertions; Jira's
   index lags unboundedly). Replaced with direct per-issue 404 polling.
8. J5: make test runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (Makefile:154) — a NEW marker
   would not be excluded. Now uses the existing `integration` marker, so no Makefile test: edit.
9. J1: external evidence needs the [operator-attested] tag (ADR 0043). Swept across all 19 tickets.

## Next actions for whoever resumes
1. Re-run `rebar review-plan 9249-1569-7be9-4f67` and `rebar review-plan c97f-90ae-4976-47c7`
   SERIALLY, once the Anthropic API is healthy. Check cheaply first with
   `rebar review-plan <id> --status` (read-only, no LLM) — but do NOT run it while a review holds
   the lock.
2. Do not edit a ticket after it certifies; that stales the attestation (learned the hard way on S7).
3. Then work in dependency order: 061c starts at 7468 (S1) and 9249 (S7); e369 starts at acb2 (J1)
   and c97f (J5). `rebar ready` identifies unblocked tickets as prerequisites close.
4. Open question deliberately left to be answered by measurement, not assumption: whether Bedrock
   prompt caching works with a cross-region inference-profile ARN (S3/2932 AC).
5. Epic be74 (GitHub Issues sync) now inherits the store-vocabulary generalization (jira_key, the
   `jira-` id prefix, CREATION_CHANNELS) that the DC epic deliberately does not do; recorded in J8's
   ADR scope.
